 Instant observations as Sixers erase 29-point deficit to win home opener 
 October 22, 2026 | 10:02 PM EDT October 22, 2026 | 10:41 PM EDT 
 Bob Cooney 
 A Decrease font size. 
 A Reset font size. 
 A Increase font size. 
 PHILADELPHIA — How bad were the Sixers in the first half in their home opener against the Cleveland Cavaliers? So much so that the disgruntled fan base took out their frustrations on the halftime entertainment, lustily booing the act while the scoreboard showed their team down 24 points.
 How great were the Sixers in the second half? Well, if the act came back and took the court after the game, he may have gotten a standing ovation.
 The excitement that this season is expected to bring may be able to match what the last 24 minutes of the game brought, but man it’s going to be hard as the Sixers posted a stunning 114-106 win to improve to 2-0.
 Maybe a lackluster performance by the Sixers to start their home opener should have been expected after all the pomp and circumstance that enveloped the season-opener up in New York on Tuesday. Not only were the festivities of the night draining — with the Knicks getting their obnoxious rings and raising their first title banner since 1973 — so was the game. Whether they will admit it or not, it appeared to have a toll on the Sixers as they seemed completely out of sorts, and legs, in that first half. 
 Or maybe with all the talent that has been assembled on this team, comebacks from deficits as big as 29 points should be expected as everyone contributed to the most exciting home-opening win in years.
 Joel Embiid scored seven straight points in the fourth quarter, the final two giving the Sixers their first lead at 96-95. Tyrese Maxey was everything, with 32 points. Jaylen Brown (21 points, eight rebounds) showed his isolation dominance with continuous breakdowns of his defender. LeBron James, again, played like a possessed 21-year-old. VJ Edgecombe did everything else that needed to be done.
 Not only was it not good, it was downright bad in the first 24 minutes. If someone left their heart in San Francisco, the Sixers seemed to leave their legs in Madison Square Garden before they found them after the break in the wild comeback.
 Here are some looks and observations of a game that won’t soon be forgotten.
 *A nice video tribute before the starting lineups were announced of Sixer teams and players from years past.
 *For those who care, and it amazes me how many do, the order of the Sixers starting lineup announced by Matt Cord was Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Joel Embiid.
 *Boyz II Men sang the National Anthem before boxing legend Bernard Hopkins rang the bell.
 *The defense was a step slow, team basketball at the offensive end was nearly invisible, loose balls weren’t gotten at all by the Sixers.
 *A nice early sign before things got out of hand early was a sweet backdoor cut by Edgecombe that was rewarded by a beautiful bounce pass from James for a dunk.
 *Early on, the Sixers did a nice job of keeping the Cavaliers off the offensive glass. But as things got worse, the Cavaliers started getting them more and more.
 *At one point in the first half, Cleveland was 14-for-17 from the foul line while the Sixers were 3-for-4. The game finished with Cleveland going 21-for-28 and the Sixers 23-for-30.
 *The lack of movement at the offensive end by the Sixers was non-existent. Too many times players looked to just go one-on-one.
 *Embiid’s hands were not good throughout the night. He couldn’t handle high passes, low passes and couldn’t keep his dribble.
 *The Sixers had just seven assists on their first 18 made field goals. Tuesday in New York, they assisted on 28 of their 37 makes.
 *Cleveland’s Donovan Mitchell had 22 points on just nine shots in 15 minutes in the first half.
 *The Cavaliers outscored the Sixers on fast break points in the first half by 22-3.
 *You had to admire a play by Maxey in the middle of the second quarter. While Mitchell was struggling with his handle along the left sideline, Maxey full-out dove after the basketball to try and get a turnover. He did that with his team down 21 points. And he did force the turnover.
 *To start the second half, the Sixers came out on their first possession and moved bodies and ball and it led to a Brown corner three.
 *The Sixers scored nine points in the first 51 seconds of the second half. They scored the first 11 to cut the lead to 69-56.
 *It is amazing how James can get out in the open floor and still be the fastest and quickest on the break.
 *Nurse didn’t sub in the third quarter until he put Kentavious Caldwell-Pope for Brown with 4:33 to go.
 *The energy the Sixers brought out in the second half was contagious on both ends of the floor, with each player looking to defend harder, run faster and play better than his teammate.
 *The Sixers took their first lead in the second half with 6:52 to go in the game when Embiid hit a 15-foot jumper to make it 96-95. It was the seventh straight point by the center.
 *Maxey and good friend and former teammate James Harden got into it a little bit at about the six minute mark in the fourth, with both pushing each other’s hand away. Refs and players stepped in before anything could come of it.
 *Edgecombe got a pretty good bloody nose in the fourth, courtesy of an elbow from teammate James.
 *The starters again got a ton of minutes, as each played at least 32.
 *The Sixers outscored the Cavaliers by 69-37 in the second half.
 *The Sixers got just nine points from their bench.
 Bob Cooney
